title: useRef and DOM refs
summary: Refs as mutable boxes that do not trigger renders, DOM refs for focus and measurement, ref callbacks, passing refs to your own components, and when not to use a ref.

sections.title: A box that survives renders
sections.body:
`const ref = useRef(initial)` returns the same `{ current }` object on every render. Changing `ref.current` **does not re-render**. Use refs for values that the render output does not depend on: timer ids, the previous value, a flag for an in-flight request, an imperative library instance.

Do not read or write `ref.current` during rendering (except to lazily initialise it); React cannot track it, so the screen can go stale. Read and write refs in handlers and effects.

sections.title: DOM refs
sections.body:
Pass a ref to a DOM element with `ref={inputRef}`; React sets `inputRef.current` to the node after mounting and back to `null` on unmount. Use it for **imperative** work React has no prop for: focus, selection, scrolling, measuring, playing media.

A **ref callback** `ref={node => …}` runs with the node when it attaches. In React 19 it can return a cleanup function, which React calls when the node detaches.

sections.title: Refs to your own components
sections.body:
In React 19, function components receive `ref` as a normal prop, so you can pass it straight to a DOM element: `function TextInput({ ref, ...props }) { return <input ref={ref} {...props} /> }`. Before React 19 this needed `forwardRef`, which still works but is no longer necessary.

`useImperativeHandle(ref, () => ({ focus, clear }))` exposes a small custom API instead of the whole DOM node.

pitfalls: Expecting the screen to update after changing `ref.current`.
Reading `ref.current` during render, or in the first render before the DOM node exists.
Using refs to control things React can do declaratively, such as showing or hiding an element.
Calling `focus()` on a ref to a component that never attaches the ref to a DOM element.

gotchas.question: What does the button show after three clicks?
gotchas.answer: 0. Changing a ref does not re-render, so the label never updates (until something else causes a render).

gotchas.question: What is `inputRef.current` while the component first renders?
gotchas.answer: `null` (the initial value). React sets it after the DOM node is created, before layout effects and effects run.
